outputs.name: unitGuides
outputs.description: A `Guide[]` exported as `unitGuides` by `src/guides/development-tooling/units.ts`, holding exactly one guide with topic `'unit'` whose summary, steps, rules, anti-patterns and example commands explain what a unit is and how to work with a unit's contract. Read it when you need the static guidance for the unit topic; it is a constant literal in source with no runtime reads, so it is generic and does not describe any specific unit's manifest.

examples.summary: A unit is one responsibility with a stable identity, owned source and a contract.
steps: Generate the unit, or index existing source into the registry.
Replace the derived responsibility and contract with declared ones when they matter.
Declare dependencies that cross a runtime boundary: process, HTTP, Wasm or contract.
Before changing code, name the units you change and read only their source.
Read dependency contracts with harness units show instead of their implementations.
Run harness units check-contract <id> when writing or changing a contract; review each heuristic finding.
Run harness units guide <id>, write and commit the standard test for NEXT, run harness verify run --priority agent-test --entity <id>, and repeat the guide until DONE.
Re-index after every source change and commit the manifests with the code.
rules: Guide completion covers named unit catalog and dedicated scenario states. Guesses are advisory; declare a justified guess as a unit state to require its proof.
Manifests live in specification/units, one canonical JSON file per unit.
An identity never changes and is never given to different source.
Moving source keeps the identity; recreating retired source revives it with its baseline.
Retire a unit explicitly once its source is gone; the tombstone keeps its history.
runtime.kind and runtime.entry name the default execution target; runtime.targets lists every applicable target, includes the default, and names each runtime kind once.
An alternative implementation in other source is its own unit, linked to the original by a declared contract dependency.
Derived responsibilities and contracts are labelled derived until a person declares them.
A unit recreated from retired source records lineage to the retired identity, so baselines and history carry over.
Manifests cap performance tolerance at 5%; only a recorded reviewer approval changes it.
Derived dependencies come from imports; unresolved or computed imports are uncertain.
Uncertain references are reported and widen test selection until they are declared.
harness generate component stays the Svelte component scaffold; harness generate unit accepts any scaffold kind and also writes the manifest.
antiPatterns: Do not edit an identity to dodge a frozen budget.
Do not delete a manifest by hand; retire the unit.
Do not read the whole repository when the unit contracts answer the question.
exampleCommands: harness generate unit Billing --kind service --responsibility "Charges an invoice once."
